finding.claim: Admin check on /admin/users/<uid>/ban is not enforced. require_admin calls abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The broad `except Exception` catches it, logs a warning, and execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin can ban any user.
finding.source: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban by any authenticated non-admin user; uid comes from the URL

trace.note: Route handler for the ban endpoint has no other auth decorator
abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, a subclass of Exception, for a non-admin
The handler only logs a warning and does not re-raise or return

finding.guards_checked: The require_admin guard is the only one, and its result is swallowed. The sibling unban route calls it without try/except, so it is enforced there. No before_request hook or other middleware exists in the file. The log line also writes the user name to the logs, which is minor.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 on failure, but the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in try/except Exception (admin.py:18) that only logs and does not re-raise or return. No before_request hook or decorator exists. The sibling unban route (admin.py:26) calls it unguarded, so it is enforced there.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the abort(403) raised by require_admin (admin.py:11) is swallowed by `except Exception` and do_ban(uid) runs anyway, so any non-admin user who reaches the route can ban any user.
